# Best open-ear earbuds for running

I can't browse, so I can't give direct retailer links. Each link below goes to a review page that has current buy buttons.

| Pick | Best for | Price in the sources | Key specs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** | Best overall, premium clip-on | $199 (down from $299) | 7-7.5 hr battery, IPX4, physical buttons |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** | Most awareness (bone conduction) | $180 list, listed at $125 at some retailers | 12 hr battery, IP55 |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** | Long runs and bad weather | $200 | 10 hr battery (40 with case), IP57 |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** | Value, best bass | $99 at Amazon | IP54 |
| **JLab Flex Open** | Cheapest way to try the clip-on style | $40 | 7 hr battery (21 with case) |

## Why these
- **Bose Ultra Open:** Runner's World named it best overall. It has clear sound, stays put, and the speaker is aimed at the ear canal, so less sound leaks. WIRED likes the physical buttons for use while running. The downsides are the price and a battery that is only so-so. Runner's World also says Bose plans to release a new pair within a month, so you may want to wait. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2:** This is the best choice if hearing traffic is your top priority. WIRED praised the running fit, fuller bass, and physical controls. Drawbacks include some lost clarity compared with the older OpenRun, and the neckband can clash with ponytails and winter hats. WIRED's review is from 2024 and found battery life shorter than promised. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Shokz OpenDots 2:** WIRED's top overall pick. It is waterproof enough to wear in rain and submerge, and the clip leaves the top of your ear free for glasses and hats. It is pricey. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Nothing Ear (Open):** SoundGuys' top open-ear pick and its choice for best workout earbuds for running. It has strong bass for this category and a customizable EQ. [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [SoundGuys workout guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)
- **JLab Flex Open:** It has less bass and detail, and touch controls only. Runner's World's text mentions both $40 and $50, so check the price. If you want a little more, WIRED likes the $50 Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, and SoundGuys picks the Soundcore AeroFit 2 (IP55) at $79.99. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

## Quick advice
- Pick **bone conduction** (OpenRun Pro 2) if you run on busy roads. Pick a **clip-on** (Bose, OpenDots 2) if you want fuller sound and don't like a neckband.
- Open-ear designs don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.
- Prices vary and the sale prices above may have changed, so check the retailer before buying.

If you tell me your budget and whether you wear glasses, hats, or have long hair, I can narrow it to one pick.
